title: Automotive and Watercraft Service Attendants
description: Service automobiles, buses, trucks, boats, and other automotive or marine vehicles with fuel, lubricants, and accessories. Collect payment for services and supplies. May lubricate vehicle, change motor oil, refill antifreeze, or replace lights or other accessories, such as windshield wiper blades or fan belts. May repair or replace tires.

tasks.text: Perform minor repairs, such as adjusting brakes, replacing spark plugs, or changing engine oil or filters.
Grease and lubricate vehicles or specified units, such as springs, universal joints, or steering knuckles, using grease guns or spray lubricants.
Rotate, test, and repair or replace tires.
Collect cash payments from customers, and make change or charge purchases to customers' credit cards, providing customers with receipts.
Order stock, and price and shelve incoming goods.
Clean parking areas, offices, restrooms, or equipment, and remove trash.
Prepare daily reports of fuel, oil, and accessory sales.
Maintain customer records and follow up periodically with telephone, mail, or personal reminders of services due.

clusters.label: Estimating the Quantifiable Characteristics of Products, Events, or Information

tasks.text: Check tire pressure and levels of fuel, motor oil, transmission, radiator, battery, or other fluids, adding air or fluids as required.
Activate fuel pumps and fill fuel tanks of vehicles with gasoline or diesel fuel to specified levels.
Sell and install accessories, such as batteries, windshield wiper blades, fan belts, bulbs, or headlamps.
Provide customers with information about local roads or highways.

skills.name: Active Listening
skills.def: Giving full attention to what other people are saying, taking time to understand the points being made, asking questions as appropriate, and not interrupting at inappropriate times.

skills.name: Speaking
skills.def: Talking to others to convey information effectively.

skills.name: Service Orientation
skills.def: Actively looking for ways to help people.

skills.name: Operation and Control
skills.def: Controlling operations of equipment or systems.

skills.name: Time Management
skills.def: Managing one's own time and the time of others.

skills.name: Critical Thinking
skills.def: Using logic and reasoning to identify the strengths and weaknesses of alternative solutions, conclusions, or approaches to problems.

skills.name: Coordination
skills.def: Adjusting actions in relation to others' actions.

skills.name: Complex Problem Solving
skills.def: Identifying complex problems and reviewing related information to develop and evaluate options and implement solutions.

skills.name: Equipment Maintenance
skills.def: Performing routine maintenance on equipment and determining when and what kind of maintenance is needed.

skills.name: Repairing
skills.def: Repairing machines or systems using the needed tools.

skills.name: Judgment and Decision Making
skills.def: Considering the relative costs and benefits of potential actions to choose the most appropriate one.

skills.name: Social Perceptiveness
skills.def: Being aware of others' reactions and understanding why they react as they do.

skills.name: Reading Comprehension
skills.def: Understanding written sentences and paragraphs in work-related documents.

skills.name: Monitoring
skills.def: Monitoring/Assessing performance of yourself, other individuals, or organizations to make improvements or take corrective action.

skills.name: Operations Monitoring
skills.def: Watching gauges, dials, or other indicators to make sure a machine is working properly.

skills.name: Writing
skills.def: Communicating effectively in writing as appropriate for the needs of the audience.

skills.name: Persuasion
skills.def: Persuading others to change their minds or behavior.

skills.name: Negotiation
skills.def: Bringing others together and trying to reconcile differences.

skills.name: Quality Control Analysis
skills.def: Conducting tests and inspections of products, services, or processes to evaluate quality or performance.

skills.name: Internet browser software
skills.def: Software to view the contents of web pages and to navigate from one page to another. Examples: Apple Safari, Microsoft Edge, Mozilla Firefox, Web browser software.

skills.name: Spreadsheet software
skills.def: Software to create or edit numbers or text organized into rows and columns of cells. May include formulas which recalculate values based on other cells. Examples: Microsoft Excel.

skills.name: Electronic mail software
skills.def: Software to compose, send, or receive email. Examples: Microsoft Outlook.

skills.name: Operating system software
skills.def: Software to provide the operational interface to a computer and provide higher-level services and APIs. Examples: Microsoft Windows.

skills.name: Inventory management software
skills.def: Software to maintain the inventory of businesses including restaurants or retail shops. Examples: Inventory management systems.

skills.name: Development environment software
skills.def: Software to create or maintain applications which run on a computer or mobile device. Examples: Software libraries.
